title: Dedicated fleet incident: capacity shortfall and autoscaler regression postmortem
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 we observed capacity shortfalls on several Dedicated customer pools during afternoon traffic spikes. The autoscaler did not provision additional GPU nodes quickly enough, causing elevated latency and a temporary increase in 429/503 errors for affected customers. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and the postmortem action items with owners and deadlines.
timeline: 2026-03-09 14:08 UTC - Alert: autoscaler headroom < 10% for pool-dedicated-eu-2 (Grafana alert DED_POOL_HEADROOM)
2026-03-09 14:12 UTC - Traffic spike confirmed (synthetic and customer-driven). Several routes experienced 95th percentile latency increases to > 900ms.
2026-03-09 14:20 UTC - Oncall (Miguel) examined scaling logs: scaling decision evaluated but did not trigger new nodes due to target_utilization calculation returning lower-than-expected values.
2026-03-09 14:35 UTC - Manual scale-up of pool-dedicated-eu-2 by +4 nodes as emergency mitigation (kubectl patch -> infra-autoscaler). Immediate traffic stabilized.
2026-03-09 15:10 UTC - Rollback of autoscaler config change deployed earlier in the week (runtime-1.18 rollout) performed to restore previous cooldown and hysteresis behavior.
2026-03-09 18:00 UTC - Incident declared resolved for customer-facing errors; follow-up postmortem scheduled.
2026-03-10 - Root cause investigation began; load-test reproduction and log analysis started.
2026-03-12 - Confirmed regression introduced by change in autoscaler logic (PR #2321) that adjusted effective_target_utilization and extended cooldown under certain cache-miss patterns.
2026-03-13 - Hotfix PR #2349 merged to correct cooldown computation and add guardrail checks; deployed to canary and then all regions.
2026-03-14 - This postmortem ticket opened and action items assigned.
Note: updated_at is 2026-03-14 reflecting assignment of action owners and scheduling of follow-ups.
root_cause: A logic regression in the autoscaler calculation (introduced in PR runtime#2321) incorrectly combined KV-cache miss penalty with target_utilization, causing the effective_target_utilization to be underestimated during cache-warmup periods. Combined with an accidental increase in the global cooldown window (config drift during a quiet rollback), the autoscaler suppressed scale-up decisions during real traffic spikes and did not meet the throughput guarantees for Dedicated pools.
mitigations: Immediate: Manually scaled affected pools (+4 nodes each) to restore headroom and rollback autoscaler config to previous cooldown/hysteresis values (2026-03-09 14:35 - 15:10 UTC).
Short-term: Deployed hotfix PR #2349 to fix cooldown computation and add explicit guardrail that prevents effective_target_utilization < 0.3 for Dedicated pools (canary then global).
Monitoring: Added a temporary synthetic job that injects a controlled spike every 6 hours against a canary pool to validate scaling behavior under KV cache churn.
Communication: Notified affected customers and updated the status page with incident impact and ETA for fixes.
Runbook: Escalation steps added for manual scale and rollback commands; immediate oncall checklist appended.
action_items: ENG-5074: Add unit and integration tests for autoscaler target_utilization math to catch negative/unsupported values (owner: Jordan Liu, due: 2026-03-21)
ENG-5075: Implement canary gating for autoscaler config changes with synthetic spike validation job (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-28)
ENG-5076: Update Dedicated runbook with explicit manual-scaling commands, Grafana dashboard links, and post-incident checklist (owner: Miguel Santos, due: 2026-03-17)
ENG-5077: Create alert that both tracks headroom and validates autoscaler decisions (decision drift) with playbook automated suggestions (owner: Evelyn Moore, due: 2026-03-24)
ENG-5078: Short-term policy: tighten default effective_target_utilization floor for Dedicated pools to 0.35 until autoscaler is fully validated (owner: SRE Team, due: 2026-03-16)
ENG-5079: Post-deployment smoke test: nightly canary scaling validation added to CI for runtime-1.18 related changes (owner: CI Platform, due: 2026-04-01)
ENG-5080: Conduct a tabletop incident review with PMs/Support/Engineering and document customer impact and communication gaps (owner: Asha Patel, due: 2026-03-25)
ENG-5081: Add telemetry to record autoscaler-decisions-reason field for every scaling attempt to improve future RCA (owner: Data Platform, due: 2026-03-31)
Note: Each action item created as separate Linear ticket; see sub_issues.
